questions: What is the modulo value used for printing the sum of f(P) over all paths?
Is the initial grid configuration provided in the input, or is it assumed to be zero everywhere except for updates?
Are the values A_{h,w} updated immediately after each move, or are they batched until all Q changes are processed?
Does Takahashi's starting position (sh, sw) get reset after each query, or does he continue moving from his new position?
Can Takahashi move outside the bounds of the grid during any of his moves?
Is the product f(P) computed using modular arithmetic, and if so, which modulus is applied?
How exactly should ties or unspecified orderings among paths be handled when computing the final result?
Should the output include leading zeros to match a specific width, or is standard integer formatting acceptable?
answers: The result must be printed modulo 998244353.
The initial grid configuration is provided in the input.
Values are updated immediately; each update takes effect before the next query.
Takahashi continues from his new position; no reset occurs.
No. All provided moves keep Takahashi within the grid boundaries.
No unspecified orderings exist; enumerate all C(H+W-2, H-1) paths and sum their contributions.
No leading zeros required; use standard integer formatting.
inline_prompts:
There is an H \times W grid. Let (h,w) denote the cell at the h-th row from the top and the w-th column from the left. A non-negative integer A_{h,w} is written in cell (h,w).
Takahashi starts at cell (sh,sw) and will perform Q changes to the grid. The i-th change is given by a character d_i (d_i is one of L, R, U, D) and a non-negative integer a_i, meaning Takahashi will do the following:
- Move one cell in the direction d_i. That is, if d_i is L, move left; if R, move right; if U, move up; if D, move down by one cell. Then, let the destination cell be (h,w), and set A_{h,w} to a_i.
It is guaranteed that in each change, he can move one cell in direction d_i.
After each change, print the answer to the following problem:
A sequence of cells P = ((h_1,w_1), \ldots, (h_{M},w_{M})) is said to be a path if and only if it satisfies all of the following conditions:
- (h_1,w_1) = (1,1), (h_{M},w_{M}) = (H,W), and M = H + W - 1.
- For every i with 1 \leq i \leq M-1, either (h_{i+1}, w_{i+1}) = (h_i + 1, w_i) or (h_{i+1}, w_{i+1}) = (h_i, w_i + 1).
For a path P = ((h_1,w_1), \ldots, (h_{M},w_{M})), define f(P) = \prod_{1\leq i\leq M}A_{h_i,w_i}. Print the sum, modulo 998244353, of f(P) over all paths P.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
A_{1,1} \cdots A_{1,W}
\vdots
A_{H,1} \cdots A_{H,W}
Q sh sw
d_1 a_1
\vdots
d_Q a_Q
Output
Print Q lines.
The i-th line should contain the sum, modulo 998244353, of f(P) over all paths P after performing the i-th change to the grid.
Constraints
- 2 \leq H, W \leq 200000
- HW \leq 200000
- 0 \leq A_{h,w} < 9
